name: Accordion
markup: No html in this file. Each variant below carries the path to its own markup at r/accordion/<variant>.html — fetch the one you need.
description: Sections of content that collapse to their heading. The heading is a button that toggles the panel below it.
when_to_use: Several sections of one record whose headings read as a set — a vendor master split into general, bank and compliance, a QC report by check, a long form broken into stages. One trigger over one panel is not this component: that is collapsible, and a row of separate collapsibles stacked up is exactly what this entry exists to replace, because the group, the single-open rule and the heading outline all belong to something that knows there is more than one. The test is whether the headings are a list somebody reads down. Never collapse something the user has to act on to finish the task in front of them.
rules: x-collapse needs the Alpine collapse plugin loaded before Alpine core. Without it the directive is ignored and the panel never shows — drop x-collapse and the plain x-show still works, it just snaps open instead of animating. The failure looks like a styling problem and it is a script tag.
The rotate binding goes on a wrapping <span>, never on the <i data-lucide>. Lucide replaces that element with an <svg> and the binding dies with it.
Rotation needs a block-level box in Tailwind v4 — the wrapping span is flex for that reason.

The header does not change height between open and closed, or the second click lands somewhere else. That is not the same as a fixed height: a header that wraps its meta onto a second line at 390px is fine, because it wraps the same way in both states. What it may not do is grow when the panel opens.

Every panel needs an id, and its button needs aria-controls pointing at it. Without that pairing a screen reader announces a button that expands nothing. Rendered in a loop the id takes the record key — acc-lines-1187 — or the second header points at the first panel and every row opens the same section.

Never put padding on the element x-collapse animates. box-sizing is border-box, so height:0 cannot go below the padding — the panel bottoms out at the padding height and then x-show removes it in a single frame, which reads as a snap. Put the padding on an inner div, and give that div padding rather than margin: a margin on the first or last child collapses straight through the animated wrapper and the plugin measures short.

A header inside a form needs type="button". The default is submit, so the first click on a section posts a half-filled record instead of opening it, and the defect only appears once the accordion is dropped into a real form.

The root is overflow-hidden so a full-bleed header hover is clipped by the card's own corners instead of squaring them off. That clip is also why the header focus outline takes the negative offset — drawn outwards it would be cut off by the same rule.

The closed row has to say what is inside it. A count, an amount, a status dot — and anything that must survive the close, an error count or a warning, belongs on the header or in a strip beside it, never only in the panel. A section nobody opens is a section nobody reads.

Meta inside the button is part of the button's accessible name. A count or an amount reads well there; a sentence is read out on every pass through the set, so a sentence goes in a paragraph under the header instead.

A field inside a closed panel cannot take focus and cannot be reported. Native validation on a display:none required control fails with "An invalid form control is not focusable", the submit silently does nothing and the user is told nothing. Put novalidate on the form, validate in one place, and open the section before moving focus into it.

Focus after a reveal needs a frame as well as a tick. At $nextTick the panel x-show is about to unhide is still display:none, and .focus() on an unrendered element is a silent no-op that leaves the keyboard where it was.

Find-in-page does not reach an x-show panel. Ctrl-F walks rendered text and display:none is not rendered, so a term inside a closed section does not exist as far as the browser is concerned. Sections holding reference text somebody will search are the argument for <details>, which is collapsible/native.

A collapsed panel is not a permission boundary and it is not a cleared field. x-show renders the markup and hides it, so a cost breakup behind a closed header is in the page source of everyone who can load the page, and anything typed into a section that is then folded away still posts.

A panel expensive enough to defer is fetched by htmx, not by Alpine. hx-trigger="intersect once" on the body inside the panel fires the first time it is genuinely on screen — a display:none element never intersects — so the request goes out on the first open and once only.

anatomy.description: Holds the open state. One x-data for the whole group when only one panel may be open, one per item when several may.
A real button whose height does not change between states, wrapped in a heading element so the group appears in the document outline.
A chevron in a flex span. The rotation class goes on the span, never on the icon.
The collapsible region, carrying an id the header points at through aria-controls, x-show, x-cloak and nothing else — no padding, no border, no background.
The inner div holding the padding and the content, so the panel can genuinely reach height 0.
Optional right-aligned summary — a count, an amount, a status — so the row is useful while closed.
What the header carries when the section needs attention: a red dot and a count of failures, an amber phrase. It stays on the header because a shut section is one nobody is reading.
One button above the set that opens or closes all of it. Its label is derived from how many are open, and its aria-controls lists every panel id.

behaviour: Clicking the header toggles its own panel. Clicking an open header closes it.
In single-open mode, opening one panel closes the others. Track the open item by id, not by index, so reordering does not move the open state.
A panel that starts closed needs x-cloak. A panel that starts open must not have it, or it stays hidden until Alpine boots.
The header height does not change between states, so a second click always lands on the same control.

A group control expands or collapses the whole set, and its label is computed from how many are open rather than from a flag of its own. Open the last section by hand and the button has to say Collapse all, or the next press expands what is already expanded and reads as broken.
A failed submit opens the section holding the bad field and moves focus to the field, not to the header. The header is where the error count goes; the field is where the correction happens.
A locked section shows its header disabled with the reason beside it, and its content is not in the document at all.
A section with nothing in it is not a section. Render the one line that says so, rather than a control that opens onto nothing.
A section the user has to act on to finish the task is not collapsible. Draw it open, with no trigger on it.
A deferred panel is fetched on the first open and never again. The skeleton is roughly the height of the answer, so the panel does not resize under the pointer when it lands.
accessibility: The header is a button, never a div with a click handler, and inside a form it is type="button".
aria-expanded reflects the open state and is bound, not hardcoded.
aria-controls on the button matches the id on the panel. A disabled header with no panel in the document drops aria-controls rather than pointing it at an id that is not there.
Wrap the header in h3, or whichever level fits the page outline, so screen readers can jump between sections.
The chevron is decorative and carries no label — the heading text alone says what the section is.

A group control is not aria-expanded. That describes what the button itself opens, and this one opens five things — it takes aria-controls listing every panel id, space-separated, and a label that says which way the next press will go.
Meta inside the header is part of the accessible name, so it stays to a count, an amount or a status. Sentences go in a paragraph under the header, outside the button.

An invalid field inside a closed section is announced by the summary above the form, not by the section. The summary entry opens the section and then focuses the control, because a fragment link to a display:none element scrolls nowhere and focuses nothing.
